name: Name
body: The Black Tide campaign follows the return of the Orgoth to the shores of the Iron Kingdoms for the first time in 400 years. This second season sees the invaders firmly entrenched in their assault, advanced to the great cities of the Iron Kingdoms but ground to a stalemate by the grit and will of the defending armies. The impasse will be short-lived, however, as strange circumstances make for strange allies, and new forces join the struggle for the future of the Iron Kingdoms!

name: Name
body:
Black Tide is an ongoing campaign for two or more players. The campaign takes place over four seasons with each season comprised of three chapters, delivered one chapter per month via subscription to the WARMACHINE app. Each chapter is comprised of three scenarios.
When playing the Black Tide campaign, each player chooses to play as either an Invader or a Defender. If players select the same allegiance, it will be necessary for players to play games as the opposing allegiance in order to facilitate all players having the opportunity to play through the three scenarios according to their chosen allegiance. Players should divide themselves between Invaders and Defenders as evenly as possible.
Scenarios are intended to be played in order but can be repeated for campaign groups of more than two players in order to allow all players to play each scenario in the role of their chosen allegiance. It is not necessary for all players to play each other, only that all players have the opportunity to play each scenario. Players should only gain War Chest points (see below) from their best result of a specific scenario each season. So, if a player repeats a scenario, only record the results of the highest score for that scenario; do not record the points from a specific scenario more than once.

name: Name
body: Character warjacks cannot be used in this campaign through normal army construction. Instead, they are created progressively by upgrading a preset warjack through with War Chest points (see below).

name: Name
body: Over the course of the Black Tide campaign, players will receive and track War Chest points to determine their success in the campaign. War Chest points are gained based on the outcome of scenario battles described at the end of each scenario. Beginning in Season Two, War Chest points may be spent between matches on a variety of benefits. Each player will be responsible for keeping a ledger of their own War Chest points. Be sure to add any War Chest points gained during a match to your total after the match and take care to accurately subtract the appropriate War Chest points from your total when you spend them for any benefits. A printable War Chest tracking sheet can be downloaded at Black Tide Season 2 War Chest Record Sheet

name: Name
body: There are three ways to spend your War Chest points during the course of the campaign: Strategic Advantages, Campaign Command Cards, and Character Warjack Upgrades.

name: Name
body:
Players can spend up to 4 War Chest points before a match for Strategic Advantages that provide a benefit during the course of the match. A Strategic Advantage is only good for the match you buy it for and does not carry over into subsequent matches.
Some Strategic Advantages can only be taken by the Underdog in match. The Underdog is the player who has the fewest War Chest points going into the match. If players are tied with War Chest points, there is no Underdog.
Normal Strategic Advantages cost 2 War Chest points. Underdog Advantages cost 1 War Chest point. Strategic Advantages can be added to your force list after Creating a Match in the WARMACHINE app by tapping the ADVANTAGES button at the bottom of the card list.

name: Name
body:
Campaign Command Cards are Command Cards designed specifically for use in the Black Tide campaign and are not meant for play in non-campaign games. Campaign Command Cards must be unlocked for use by paying 3 War Chest points. Once unlocked, they can be used in any subsequent game. Note that some Campaign Command Cards also have army point costs like other Command Cards.
Be sure to record any Campaign Command Cards you unlock so you know what is available to your force in later matches.
Campaign Command Cards will appear in your normal Command Card list in the WARMACHINE app and can be identified by the presence of "[CAMPAIGN]" in the title of the card.

name: Name
body:
In the Black Tide campaign, players using MKIV armies can use War Chest points to upgrade character warjacks. Character warjacks start with a stock loadout and can be upgraded over time by spending War Chest points. Each upgrade costs 3 War Chest points, and once an upgrade is purchased, it is a permanent change to the warjack for all subsequent matches. The benefit to upgrading a character warjack in this fashion is that the upgrades do not change the army point cost of the warjack, so as you upgrade it, the warjack gets a more valuable loadout, which is then permanently available to your force at a bargain cost.
When upgrading a character warjack, both arm weapons must be upgraded before the head can be upgraded. And the head must be upgraded before a bond can be selected. Once an upgrade is purchased, including a bond, it cannot be changed for the duration of the campaign.
Be sure to record your character warjack upgrades when you spend your War Chest points on them.

name: Name
body: When setting up to play Black Tide scenarios, players will take turns placing terrain on the table as described by the scenario. When placing terrain features, a player cannot place an obstacle or obstruction within 5" of another obstacle or obstruction.

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective uncontested.

name: Name
body: Scenario victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set number of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
Some Black Tide scenarios are designated as key battles. These are particularly large or important battles to the narrative of the campaign. Key Battle scenarios are noted in the title of the scenario. A player who wins a Key Battle scenario gains an additional War Chest point.
Players who are participating in the Resurrection League may choose to include the league model, Reinholdt, Gobber Spy, as part of their force. If they do, they may undertake a Gobber Spy mission during the Key Battles of this campaign to earn additional Victory Points. Gobber Spy missions are detailed in the Key Battle scenarios.

name: Name
body: As the frozen landscape yielded to the tentative whispers of an imminent spring, Major Anson Wolfe, the resolute leader of Cygnar’s Storm Legion, found himself entangled in a desperate gambit against the relentless Orgoth invaders. Every effort to erect defenses crumbled beneath the Orgoth’s relentless assault, and every step of the strategic retreat that followed weighed heavily on Wolfe’s tormented soul. He was a seasoned tactician, and he grappled painfully with the dire necessity of ceding ground. Every inch surrendered brought the Orgoth closer to Cygnar while a motley assembly of Cygnaran, Khadoran, and Dusk forces stood united against the unyielding onslaught. Each retreating footfall heightened the stakes, but Wolfe knew that digging in only meant certain annihilation. As the allied forces retreated, his mind raced, calculating the perilous gamble that lay ahead. The Orgoth, in relentless pursuit, pressed forward with their insatiable hunger for conquest. But Wolfe’s heart bore the burden of sacrifice for the heavy price paid to lure the invaders into the intricately laid traps and the waiting artillery positioned in their path.

name: Name
body: Every forward step of the retreat was a heartbeat echoing with the anguish of forsaking the land he had vowed to defend. Yet it was a calculated sacrifice, a desperate attempt to stall the Orgoth menace. The inevitable battle would be pivotal in determining Cygnar’s fate, if not the fate of all the Iron Kingdoms. As the Orgoth closed in, Wolfe directed his forces with precision. The treacherous landscape became a canvas for their trap, an intricate web woven to ensnare the pursuers. Hidden trenches, concealed explosives, and expertly positioned snipers awaited the invaders’ advance. Wolfe’s mind churned with the gravity of his decision. To confront the Orgoth directly meant death, but from the shadows of this strategic retreat, a glimmer of hope emerged. The gambit was perilous, a high-stakes wager based on the vulnerability of the Orgoth, and Wolfe knew the cost of failure could spell doom for all. As the first echoes of battle reverberated across the desolate landscape, he steeled himself for the clash ahead. The Orgoth, blinded by their hunger for conquest, walked into the snare. And the fate of Cygnar and its allies hung in the balance.

name: Name
body: Major Anson Wolfe’s gaze surveyed the battleground with a mix of grim determination and strategic foresight. The Invaders, preparing for their final assault, faced a formidable obstacle—a series of gun emplacements strategically positioned to rain fire down upon their approaching forces. Wolfe knew these artillery positions were the linchpin of their defense. In response, the Invaders had unleashed strike forces, weaving through the treacherous terrain to spike, destroy, and silence the Defenders’ guns.

name: Name
body:
As the Invaders prepare for their final assault on the Defenders, they must first clear a number of obstacles from their planned path of attack. Chief amongst these are a number of gun emplacements that can rain fire down upon their approaching forces. To counter this threat, the Invaders have unleashed strike forces to spike, destroy, or otherwise silence the Defender’s guns.
This scenario ends after six rounds. (After six rounds, the Defender will have time to get their heavy guns loaded and trained on the Invader forces.)

name: Name
body:
The Defender builds a 75-point army.
The Invader builds a 75-point army.

name: Name
body:
Place a guard tower and three bunkers as shown on the map. The bunkers are gun emplacements.
The Defender deploys to an area 7" forward of the north table edge.
The Invader deploys to an area 10" forward of the south table edge.
Players then take turns each placing up to four additional non-building terrain features. These terrain features cannot be placed within a Deployment Zones or within 4" of another terrain feature.
The Invader cannot place defenses when playing this scenario.
The Defender deploys first, and the Invader takes the first turn.

name: Name
body:
Starting with the Defender’s second turn, a player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each Bunker or Guard Tower they are securing.
The Invader also scores 2 Victory Points each time a Bunker is destroyed.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If all three Bunkers are simultaneously destroyed and/or held by the Invader, the Invader wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points. If the Invader has not won after 6 rounds, the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: Fueled by the urgency of impending doom, Wolfe discerns the Invaders’ tactical ploys. Determined not to be mere pawns in their enemy’s calculated game, the Defenders launch a series of audacious attacks to disrupt and harry the Invaders. In a critical mission, their objective is clear—destroy a vital bridge crucial to the Invaders’ planned assault. Wolfe knows the significance; the bridge’s destruction will constrict the Invaders’ troop movements, fracturing their strategic cohesion during the impending clash. With relentless resolve, the Defenders embark on this perilous mission, a daring gambit to tip the scales in their favor and disrupt the Invaders’ meticulously laid plans.

name: Name
body:
The Invader’s preparations for their pending attack have tipped their hand to the Defenders. Refusing to wait for a time and place of their enemy’s choosing for battle, the Defenders have launched their own attacks to harass the Invaders. In this mission, the Defenders seek to destroy a bridge vital to the Invaders’ plan of attack. If the bridge can be destroyed, it will constrain the Invaders’ troop movements during their main assault.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender builds a 75-point army.
The Invader builds a 75-point army.

name: Name
body:
See the map below. A wide river spans the area of the table starting 10" from the north table edge and ending 13" from the south table edge. Lay down fifteen 3"x 5" cards as shown on the map to represent Bridge Section objectives.
The Defender deploys to an area 7" forward of the north table edge.
The Invader deploys to an area 10" forward of the south table edge.
Players then take turns each placing up to two additional terrain features. A player must place these terrain features  within their own Deployment Zones and not on or within 4" of the bridge, the river, or another terrain feature.
Neither player can place defenses when playing this scenario.
The Invader deploys first, and the Defender takes the first turn.

name: Name
body: The Bridge – The Bridge is divided into fifteen 3" x 5" Bridge Section terrain objectives, arranged in three columns of five rows each. Each Bridge Section has DEF 5, ARM 18, and 20 damage boxes. Bridge Sections are automatically hit by melee attacks. A model can target a Bridge Section with an attack if the nearest edge of the Bridge Section is within the weapon’s range. When a Bridge Section is destroyed, it is removed from the table to reveal the River beneath, but the models that were on it remain in play (and are now in the River). The River – The River is considered to be rough terrain. Continuous effects on a model completely within the River expire. A knocked-down model without Amphibious that is completely within the area of the River is removed from play. A model without Amphibious or Flight that ends its activation completely within the River is also removed from play.

name: Name
body:
Starting with the Invader’s second turn, a player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each Bridge Section they are securing. When determining which models contest a given Bridge Section, only count those models within the area of the section.
The Defender also scores 1 Victory Point each time a Bridge Section is destroyed.

name: Name
body:
Decisive Win: If at least one Bridge Section in each of the five rows is destroyed, the Bridge teeters and collapses, and the Defender wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points. If the Defender has not won after 6 rounds, the Invader wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points. A Defender with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent can choose to forgo this victory condition that turn.
(Tip: A Defender attempting a Decisive Win may wish to do this.)
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the only Leader model that has not been destroyed or removed from play wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader that has not been destroyed or removed from play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 2 War Chest points.

name: Name
body: Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.

name: Name
body: As the ominous hour of the Invaders’ final assault looms, Major Anson Wolfe contemplates the battlefield’s intricate dance. The preceding clashes, in which the Defenders fought valiantly to retain their artillery and succeeded in demolishing the vital bridge, now shape the impending doom. If the Defenders’ guns were silenced in the skirmishes leading up to this pivotal moment, their once-mighty artillery stands silent, leaving a void in their defensive arsenal. Conversely, the bridge’s destruction hampers the Invaders’ ability to reinforce their position during the final assault. The echoes of strategic gambits reverberate, and Wolfe, burdened by the weight of every calculated move, braces for the climactic clash that will determine the fate of Cygnar and its desperate Defenders.

name: Name
body:
The time has come for the Invader’s final assault. The exact details of this offensive will be defined by the battles that led up to it. If the Defender’s guns were silenced, they will not have them now to repel the Invader. If the bridge the Invader intended to cross in their attack has been destroyed, they will not be able to reinforce their position.
This scenario ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body:
The Defender builds a 75-point army.
The Invader builds a 100-point army.

name: Name
body:
See the map below. The battlefield is dominated by a peninsula that extends in a 34" radius from the northeast corner of the table. This peninsula is also the Defender’s Deployment Zone. Narrow spits of land 6" wide run along the northern and eastern table edges.
The rest of the battlefield is the Bay. The Bay is considered to be deep water (see below).
The Defender places some combination of eight Bunkers, Guard Towers, and Trenches anywhere within their Deployment Zone. A Bunker or Guard Tower cannot be placed within 4" of a table edge or another Bunker or Guard Tower.
The Defender can then place up to two additional terrain features that cannot include Bunkers, Guard Towers, or Trenches anywhere within their Deployment Zone. These terrain features cannot be placed within 4" of a table edge or another non-Trench terrain feature.
The Invader then places three 6" x 8" landing crafts within the area of the Bay.  Landing crafts must be placed in contact with either the south or west table edges and cannot be placed within 12" of the north or east table edges.

name: Name
body:
The Invader cannot place defenses in this scenario.
The Defender deploys first and takes the first turn.
All models lose Advance Deployment and Ambush when playing this scenario.
The Invader has two 6" x 6" Deployment Zones on the narrow spits of land on either side of the peninsula. If the Invader lost the Rough Waters scenario, however, they can only deploy their models to one of these Deployment Zones. The Invader can choose which Deployment Zone when they deploy their models.
The Invader can also deploy their models onto any of the three landing crafts.

name: Name
body: Deep Water – The Bay is considered to be rough terrain. Continuous effects on a model completely within the Bay expire. A knocked-down model without Amphibious that is completely within the area of the River is removed from play. A model without Amphibious or Flight that ends its activation completely within the Bay is also removed from play. Landing Crafts – A landing craft has DEF 8, ARM 18, and has 25 damage boxes. If a landing craft is destroyed, it is removed from the table, but the models that were on it remain in play. During the Invader’s Maintenance Phase, the Invader can move each landing craft up to eight inches. A model completely within the area of a landing craft is considered to have cover and gains Resistance: Blast. Support Fire – If the Defender won the Silencer scenario, they still maintain heavy gun emplacements overlooking the battlefield and can attack with them throughout the battle. If the Defender lost the Silencer scenario, their guns were neutralized and will not be a factor in this battle.

name: Name
body: If the Defender won the Silencer scenario, starting with the Defender’s second turn, the Defender can make d3 artillery barrages at the end of each of their Control Phases. An artillery barrage can target any enemy model or landing craft on the table outside of the Defender’s Deployment Zone. An artillery barrage is a RAT 5, AOE 3, POW 14/8 ranged attack. Hoard Revenant Mission: Players who include the Hoard Revenant in their force can undertake the following covert missions: Defender: Hallowed Ground — The Hoard Revenant can make a Hallowed Ground special action once per game while completely within the Defender’s Deployment Zone and within 6" of an enemy model. When he does so, the Defender scores 1 Victory Point and all of the Invader’s upkeep spells within 10" of the Hoard Revenant expire. This action can only be taken once per game. Invader: Tomb Robber — The Hoard Revenant can make a Tomb Robber special action once per game while completely within the area of the Defender’s Deployment Zone. When he does so, the Invader scores 1 Victory Point and one friendly model within 10" of the Hoard Revenant gains 1 corpse token, essence point, focus point, fury point, rage token, or soul token. This action can only be taken once per game.

name: Name
body:
Starting with the Invader’s third turn, a player scores 1 Victory Point at the start of each of their turns for each Bunker, Guard Tower, or Trench template they are securing.
The Defender also scores 1 Victory Point each time a landing craft is destroyed.
The Invader scores 2 Victory points each time a Bunker or Guard Tower is destroyed.

name: Name
body:
If all Bunkers and Guard Towers have been destroyed, or if the Invader simultaneously holds all remaining Bunkers, Guard Towers, and Trenches, the Invader wins the match and receives 6 War Chest points.
If the Invader has not won after 6 rounds, the Defender wins the match and receives 6 War Chest points.
Point Advantage Win: At the beginning of any of their turns, a player with 5 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match and receives 5 War Chest points.
Last Leader Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with the last Leader model in play wins the match and receives 4 War Chest points.
Victory Point Win:  If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match and receives 3 War Chest points.
Tie or Loss: If the match ends in a tie, both players receive 1 War Chest point. A player receives 1 War Chest point for a loss.
